### Mirum Pharmaceuticals Announces Primary Endpoint Met in AZURE-4 Phase 3 Study and Highlights Long-Term Brelovitug Data Presented at AASLD


November 10, 2026


*–* *Phase 3 AZURE-4 primary endpoint of combined virologic response and ALT normalization at Week 24 achieved by 59% with brelovitug 300 mg once weekly*


*– Brelovitug achieved 100% virologic response and 100% ALT normalization in patients with cirrhosis following up to 108 weeks of treatment, as presented at The Liver Meeting®*


*– Favorable safety and tolerability profiles observed across all studies; no new safety signals*


*– U.S. FDA BLA submission expected in H1 2027*


FOSTER CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today announced that the primary endpoint was met in the Phase 3 AZURE-4 study evaluating brelovitug, an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody that binds to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV). AZURE-4 is the second of two Phase 3 studies that will form the basis of Mirum's U.S. registration package for brelovitug. Mirum also highlighted brelovitug data presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases’ (AASLD) The Liver Meeting®. Across three presentations, the data demonstrated deepening viral suppression, increased rates of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization, and improvements in liver stiffness with longer brelovitug treatment, including in patients with advanced cirrhosis.


“AZURE-4 marks the second U.S. registrational Phase 3 study in which brelovitug met the primary endpoint of combined virologic response and ALT normalization, demonstrating consistent efficacy in patients with substantial disease burden, including higher baseline viral loads and ALT levels,” said Nancy Shulman, M.D., Executive Vice President of Clinical Development at Mirum. “Together with the favorable safety and tolerability profiles observed across both AZURE studies and the deepening responses observed with longer-term treatment in our Phase 2 studies, we believe these results support the potential of brelovitug as a potent, single-agent treatment for chronic HDV and our planned Biologics License Application (BLA) submission in the first half of 2027.”


“Hepatitis delta is the most severe form of viral hepatitis, and many patients are living with advanced liver disease, including cirrhosis,” said Tatyana Kushner, M.D., MSCE, Associate Professor of Medicine, Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at Weill Cornell Medicine. “New 2026 AASLD expert opinion (EXPO) recommendations recognize that all adults with HDV viremia and compensated liver disease, including compensated cirrhosis, should be considered for HDV-specific antiviral therapy. The improvements in viral suppression, ALT normalization, and liver stiffness observed with brelovitug treatment are encouraging for patients facing significant risk of disease progression.”


**Phase 3 AZURE-4 Results: Brelovitug Met the Primary Endpoint at Week 24**


The AZURE-4 study enrolled 113 treatment-naïve patients randomized 2:1:1 to receive brelovitug 300 mg self-administered once weekly (QW) by subcutaneous (SC) injection, brelovitug 900 mg administered once every four weeks (Q4W) by SC injection, or delayed treatment starting at Week 12. The global study population had substantial disease burden: 53% had cirrhosis, approximately half had baseline HDV RNA levels >6 log10 IU/mL, and mean baseline ALT was 122 U/L.


At Week 24, brelovitug met the primary endpoint, with 59% of patients receiving 300 mg QW and 44% receiving 900 mg Q4W achieving the combined endpoint of virologic response and ALT normalization, compared with 0% in the delayed-treatment arm (p≤0.0001 for both comparisons).

** Virologic response is defined as ≥2 log10 reduction in HDV RNA from baseline, HDV RNA below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ, <10 IU/mL), or undetectable HDV RNA (TND).*


*** TND: Target not detected, defined as no detectable HDV RNA using an RT-qPCR assay (Victorian Infectious Diseases Reference Laboratory; Melbourne, Australia), with a limit of detection of 5 IU/mL.*


In the Phase 3 AZURE-4 study, brelovitug was well tolerated across dose groups, with no new safety signals observed. The most common adverse event was flu-like illness, reported in 17.2% and 18.5% of participants receiving 300 mg QW and 900 mg Q4W, respectively, with the majority occurring following the first dose. Low rates of injection site reactions were reported in 1.7% and 7.4% of participants, respectively.


Full results from the Phase 3 AZURE-4 study will be presented at an upcoming medical congress. Detailed analyses presented at The Liver Meeting are available in the Publications & Presentations section of[Mirum’s website](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmirumpharma.com%2Four-science%2Fpublications-presentations%2F&esheet=54638770&newsitemid=20261110113586&lan=en-US&anchor=Mirum%26%238217%3Bs+website&index=1&md5=76ff85601ccc4826ba63302c08af5216) .


Mirum plans to submit a BLA to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the first half of 2027, with a potential U.S. commercial launch in Q4 2027, if approved.


**About Chronic Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV)**


HDV, an infection that occurs in some people infected with the hepatitis B virus, is the most severe form of viral hepatitis due to the potential for rapid progression to liver cirrhosis, liver cancer, and liver-related death. HDV affects approximately 230,000 people in the United States and Europe. It is estimated that more than 50% of individuals with HDV will die of liver-related causes within 10 years of diagnosis. There are currently no approved treatments for HDV in most countries worldwide.


**About Brelovitug**


Brelovitug is an investigational, highly potent, pan-genotypic, fully human immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) that targets the surface antigen (anti-HBsAg) on both the hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and the hepatitis B virus (HBV). Brelovitug is designed to neutralize and remove hepatitis B and hepatitis D virions and deplete HBsAg-containing subviral particles. Brelovitug has FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of chronic HDV and Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of active hepatitis delta virus infection. Brelovitug also has PRIME and Orphan designations from the European Medicines Agency.


In September 2026, Mirum announced that the Phase 3 AZURE-1 study met its primary combined endpoint of virologic response and ALT normalization at Week 24, with brelovitug demonstrating a favorable safety and tolerability profile. Brelovitug is currently being evaluated in the global Phase 3 AZURE clinical program. Mirum owns worldwide rights to brelovitug.


**About the AZURE Clinical Program**


The AZURE program is a global, registrational Phase 3 clinical development program evaluating brelovitug for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The program includes multiple open-label studies designed to assess the primary endpoint of combined virologic response and ALT normalization. Together, the studies are intended to support regulatory filings in the United States and Europe.


**About AZURE-4**


AZURE-4 is a Phase 3 study evaluating brelovitug in chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The study enrolled 113 treatment-naïve patients randomized in a 2:1:1 ratio to receive brelovitug 300 mg self-administered once weekly (QW) by subcutaneous (SC) injection, brelovitug 900 mg administered once every four weeks (Q4W) by SC injection, or 12-week delayed therapeutic start. Patients randomized to delayed treatment initiate brelovitug 300 mg QW upon completion of the 12-week treatment-delay period.


The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients achieving a combined virologic response and ALT normalization at Week 24 in the 300 mg QW arm. The study includes an open-label extension period of up to 96 weeks.


**About Mirum Pharmaceuticals**


Mirum Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: MIRM) is a leading rare disease company with a global footprint of approved products and a broad pipeline of investigational medicines. Purpose-built to bring forward breakthrough medicines for people with overlooked conditions, Mirum focuses on rare liver and rare genetic diseases, where it has built deep expertise and strong connections to patient communities. The company’s commercial portfolio includes LIVMARLI® (maralixibat) for Alagille syndrome (ALGS) and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis **** (PFIC), **** ATEBRIOZ *®* (zilurgisertib) for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), CHOLBAM® (cholic acid) for bile acid synthesis disorders and CTEXLI® (chenodiol) for cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX).


Mirum’s clinical-stage pipeline includes volixibat, an IBAT inhibitor in late-stage development for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), brelovitug, a fully human monoclonal antibody in late-stage development for chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) and MRM-3379, a PDE4D inhibitor being evaluated for Fragile X syndrome (FXS).
